criteria.title: Scope: seat map, all-or-nothing holds, payment, release, waiting room

levels.0: Only 'book a ticket', with no holds or expiry.
levels.1: Covers seat selection, holds and payment, but never says holds are all-or-nothing, never sets a per-account limit, or leaves out the waiting room.
levels.2: Browse with live availability, all-or-nothing holds of up to 4 seats for 10 minutes, payment through the PSP, on-time release, and a waiting room that tells late arrivals early; resale and dynamic pricing out of scope.

criteria.title: No double sale, hold accuracy and fairness

levels.1: States 'never sell a seat twice' but not what fair means or what must happen to a hold while payment is in flight.
levels.2: No seat sold twice, holds released within seconds but never during a payment, never charge without a ticket, survive twice the forecast crowd, and a definition of fairness that defeats fastest-refresh-wins.

criteria.title: Arrivals, admission rate and sell-out time

levels.0: No numbers, or treats 1M arrivals as 1M bookings.
levels.1: Derives 16,667 joins/s but never connects the admission rate to inventory or notices most arrivals leave empty-handed.
levels.2: 16,667 joins/s (33,333 at 2x), 100,000 polls/s, 10,000 active shoppers admitted at 2,000/min, about 21 minutes to sell 25,000 orders, about 958,000 people who must be told early, and the counterfactual of 200,000 req/s and 33,000 conflicting writes/s without a waiting room.

levels.1: Sizes the front door but not the inventory writes, or sizes the database for the full crowd.
levels.2: About 100 seat writes/s (67 holds, 20 confirms, 13 releases), 2,000 seat-map reads/s, 42 waiting-room instances, 6 queue-store nodes, 21 booking API instances, and one Postgres primary at ρ ≈ 0.07, each sized for a zone loss.

levels.1: Separate hold and pay calls, but no idempotency keys, no expiry in the response, or no status for an unknown payment.
levels.2: Join returning a signed token, one shared CDN-cached now-serving file, hold with Idempotency-Key returning expiresAt from the server clock and 409 with taken seats, pay returning 200, 202 'processing' or 410 'hold expired'.

criteria.title: Seat rows, holds and orders in a transactional store

levels.0: Seat counts per section with no per-seat state.
levels.1: Per-seat rows, but holds live only in a cache or the store choice is unjustified.
levels.2: Per-seat status (available, held, paying, sold) with hold id and expiry in Postgres for all-or-nothing conditional updates, orders keyed for PSP idempotency, a separate key-value queue store, and Redis bitmaps that are derived and never authoritative.

criteria.title: Waiting room, admission, hold, pay and expiry flows

levels.0: Fans go straight to the booking service and database.
levels.1: Has a queue in front, but admission is not tied to inventory or the payment and expiry flows are missing.
levels.2: Join with one token per account, CDN polling of one shared file, an admission controller pacing by active shoppers and unsold seats, conditional holds, pay with a paying state and outbox, and a sweeper; with a latency budget.

levels.0: Read-then-write with no lock or condition.
levels.1: Uses SELECT FOR UPDATE or a version check correctly but cannot compare them, or relies on Redis SETNX as the record.
levels.2: Compares pessimistic, optimistic, single conditional update and Redis; explains READ COMMITTED re-evaluation, deadlock ordering, SKIP LOCKED for best-available, and why asynchronous Redis replication rules it out as the record.

criteria.title: Holds as leases with on-time release

levels.0: Holds never expire, or expire via application-server timers.
levels.1: Uses a TTL or a sweeper, but correctness depends on the sweeper running on time or on several machine clocks.
levels.2: Lazy expiry in the hold condition so correctness never waits for a job, an idempotent sweeper for visibility, the database clock as the only clock, and per-account hold limits against bots.

levels.1: A FIFO queue with a per-user position API that itself takes 100,000 req/s.
levels.2: Random order for the lobby and arrival order after opening, a shared CDN-cached threshold, signed account-bound tokens, admission paced by inventory, early sold-out notice, and edge-issued tokens or a lottery as alternatives.

levels.0: Releases seats when the PSP times out.
levels.1: Keeps seats during payment but has no bound or no plan for authorizations that arrive late.
levels.2: Paying state that freezes the hold, authorize then confirm then capture, decline returns to held, unknown resolved by status checks keyed by order_id, and a bounded wait after which seats are released and late authorizations voided.

levels.1: Mentions database failover but not what the queue and existing holds experience, or what breaks first at 10x.
levels.2: A primary-failover timeline that pauses admission and extends holds by the outage; at 10x names the queue store and waiting-room service first, edge tokens, longer polls far back, sharding inventory by event, and lotteries as policy.

levels.1: Generic trade-offs not tied to ticketing.
levels.2: Each key choice (waiting room, lobby lottery, shared now-serving file, Postgres conditional update, lazy expiry, paying state, auth then capture, separate queue store) with the alternative and why it lost here.
